The common advice to serve red wine at "room temperature" is misleading in modern contexts, as multiple sources clarify that the original "room temperature" referred to cooler European conditions of 60-65°F (15-18°C), not today's typical indoor temperatures of 70°F or higher [d4][d5]. According to WSET, a reputable wine education body, "room temperature for wines" is actually 15-18°C (59-64°F), and full-bodied reds served above 18°C (64°F) can lose freshness and their flavor structure can become muddled [d6]. Decanter similarly advises that lighter summer reds should be served at 10°C-16°C (50°F-60°F) and recommends refrigerating them for 30 minutes before serving [d2]. More specifically, full-bodied reds are best at 64-65°F, medium-bodied reds at 60-62°F, and light-bodied reds at 55-60°F, meaning most reds benefit from some degree of chilling relative to a typical modern room [d1]. For specific varieties like Cabernet Sauvignon, an ideal serving temperature of around 57-60°F is recommended, requiring a brief rest in the refrigerator if stored at room temperature [d3]. In warmer climates, the need to chill red wine before serving is even more pronounced, as the "room temperature" guideline simply does not apply [d7].
